surfaces.part: front face with red slot, green button and dark output strip

answer.evidence: Rows 1-5 form a light top band (L 167, 208, then 247 for rows 3-5). Row 6 is a darker 1-row front-edge line (L about 145). Rows 7-8 are a dark shadow band (L 66) directly below it. The front face then runs from row 7 to row 28 with a red slot, a green button and a dark tray strip, so it is 22 rows tall. Rows 29-30 are the dark base outline. No side face is drawn. The top band is fairly thin and could be read as a front-facing header strip, but it has both an edge line and a shadow below it, which meets evidence (a).

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate is a narrow standing machine with a pale panel, a red band and a green emblem. The measured facts are in line with the references. It has 15 visible tones per full tile, against 9 for the hedge, 17 for the cheese stall and 20 for the well. Near-flat coverage is 0%, and 0% of its dark edge pixels are neutral, so the outline carries a tint rather than being a black sticker line. By eye, the pale body is shaded with a few steps (light, mid and dark) and has a darker tinted edge, and the emblem and band add detail. It has fewer raw colours than the stall and well (22 in total), but it is a small single-tile-wide piece, so that is expected. It is a little simpler than the roofed well or cheese stall. It does not look thinner or flatter than the references, so I judge it acceptable next to them.

surfaces.part: top band / header of the dispenser

answer.evidence: Rows 1-5 form a light band at the top (L 167, 208, then 247). Row 6 is a transitional edge line (L about 147), and rows 7-8 are dark (L 66), which fits an eave shadow. Below that the blue-grey front face runs from row 6 to row 28 and holds the red display (rows 9-10), the green button (rows 15-19), the dark slot (rows 23-24) and the white tray (rows 25-27). Rows 29-30 are a dark base. The silhouette is 12 px wide throughout, so no side face is drawn. This is a borderline case: the top band could instead be read as a flat header panel, since the edge line at row 6 is only intermediate in lightness and the dark rows 7-8 may be the display frame. I counted the band as a top surface because it has an edge line followed by a dark band.
